title: Sanchi: Reading the Gateways

endcard.line: Pictures: Arnold Betten (public domain); Arian Zwegers (CC BY 2.0); Biswarup Ganguly (CC BY 3.0)

segments.say: On a hill in Madhya Pradesh stands one of India's oldest stone buildings: the Great Stupa of Sanchi. Its four gateways are a storybook in stone.
The first stupa was built of brick under Ashoka in the third century BCE. It was later enlarged in stone, and the four gateways, called toranas, came in the first century BCE.
Look closely. The panels tell stories from the Buddha's life and his past lives, the Jatakas.
But you won't find the Buddha's face. Early artists showed him only through symbols: a tree for his enlightenment, a wheel for his first sermon, footprints for his presence.
This panel shows Queen Maya's dream before his birth: an elephant, not a baby.
Inscriptions on the stones name hundreds of donors: monks, nuns, ordinary families, and even the ivory carvers of nearby Vidisha.
For GS One: Ashoka's stupa, gateways from the first century BCE, and the Buddha shown only through symbols.

sources: Archaeological Survey of India, 'Buddhist Monuments at Sanchi' (asi.nic.in): Great Stupa originally a brick structure of Ashoka's time; enlarged and encased in stone in the 2nd century BCE; four gateways of the 1st century BCE; carved with Jataka tales and scenes from the Buddha's life
UNESCO World Heritage List, 'Buddhist Monuments at Sanchi' (inscribed 1989)
NCERT Class 12 History, 'Themes in Indian History I', ch. 4 (Thinkers, Beliefs and Buildings): symbols for the Buddha; donor inscriptions including the ivory workers of Vidisha

quiz.q: When were Sanchi's carved gateways added?
quiz.why: After the stone casing, in the 1st century BCE.
